title: Rabbi Joey Soffer: Mesilat Yesharim class #10

chapters.title: Physical actions waking up internal spiritual desire
David Hamelech's psukim on yearning for Hashem
Acquiring zirizut and its connection to zehirut
chapters.about: Perek Het, emsa'im, zehirut, mitzvot aseh

chapters.title: Recognizing Hashem's daily goodness
chapters.about: tovot, gratitude, recognizing debt to Hashem

chapters.title: Three categories of motivation for avodat Hashem
Obstacles to zirizut and the danger of laziness
chapters.about: Perek Tet, mafsidei hazirizut, comfort, pampering

chapters.title: The path of a worker and Pirkei Avot on Torah
chapters.about: amal, workers, Pirkei Avot, bread and salt

summary: Rabbi Soffer goes through the final section of Perek Zayin of Mesilat Yesharim, discussing how physical actions and proactive movement inspire internal spiritual excitement and the desire for mitzvot. He then explores Perek Het and the beginning of Perek Tet, detailing how to acquire zirizut through recognizing Hashem's constant goodness and identifying the dangers of laziness and the pursuit of physical comfort.
questions: How can physical actions of a mitzvah influence your internal spiritual feelings?
What are the main ways to acquire the trait of zirizut according to the Ramchal?
Why does recognizing Hashem's daily goodness prevent laziness in avodat Hashem?
What role does the pursuit of physical comfort and rest play in diminishing zirizut?
What does Pirkei Avot teach about the lifestyle required for acquiring Torah?
